prize_parts.citation: for measuring intergenerational mobility and the causal effects of place with population-scale administrative data

statement.case_for: Intergenerational mobility became a measurable, place-specific quantity because linked population administrative data were used together with credible causal designs, such as movers and exposure effects and re-analysis of an experiment. Measurement and identification are done jointly, and that combination is what I weight most heavily across fields. The work has changed research in public, labour and urban economics. It has also changed how policymakers discuss opportunity. I move from my opening trio (Chetty, Hendren, Katz) to Chetty, Hendren and Friedman. Friedman's role in the tax-record data infrastructure and the mobility studies fits the discovery as described on this ballot entry, while Katz's most distinctive contribution is the skill-demand and wage-structure work. That work belongs with B038 rather than here.
statement.case_against: The programme is young by prize standards, with core results from about 2014 onward. Causal interpretation of neighbourhood effects and the stability of place-based estimates are still being tested. Much of the evidence rests on restricted or proprietary administrative data, so independent replication is limited. Credit is concentrated in one large, team-based research group, and a three-name cap cannot reflect that fully. It would also be fair to ask whether this is one discovery or a series of data-driven empirical contributions.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B038 first and B002 second. She notes that B002 is early, that credit is concentrated in a single group, and that dependence on restricted administrative data limits independent replication.
responses.response: The data-access concern is real and I count it against B002. It matters less for the causal claims that rest on movers and on re-analysis of a randomised experiment, because those designs can be assessed on their logic. For the descriptive patterns, similar register-based studies in other countries are the natural test. I have not verified here how closely they agree. I accept the concentration of credit and the youth of the programme as weaknesses. They explain why I treat B038 as the closest competitor and list it as an alternative, rather than as a settled preference.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B012 first with a two-person core (Kiyotaki, Moore). He leaves Katz off B002 as a less natural fit, and he flags that B002 may be too recent for the committee.
responses.response: I agree on Katz and have changed my B002 names accordingly. On B012 I also withdraw my opening inclusion of Gertler. Boppart, Krusell and Stromberg are right that the financial-accelerator strand is a partly separate line, and that Bernanke's 2022 recognition makes the credit there less clean. A two-person Kiyotaki–Moore prize is the stronger form of B012. I still disagree with ranking it above B002. The collateral-constraint mechanism is mature and foundational, but its direct empirical identification is mixed. B002's evidence is more transparent, even though it is younger.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B038 first. She credits the China-shock programme to Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and she asks whether the trade-shock and task strands form one coherent prize.
responses.response: I agree that the China-shock work is the cleanly attributable core, and I have kept the Autor–Dorn–Hanson trio as my own B038 proposal. Its design quality is close to what I value in B002. A prize on B038 would need a citation limited to that trade-shock contribution. The task-framework lineage is shared with Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu, and the 2024 prize overlaps with the latter, so it should not be folded in. The shift-share identification debate and the argument over persistence are the remaining reasons I rank it below B002. Her argument has raised B038 as an alternative in my view.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B001 first. He argues that Rubinstein's alternating-offers result is foundational and fully mature, so the main risk is that recognition is overdue rather than premature.
responses.response: I accept the scientific standing of B001 and have no doubt about its validity. That is why it was third in my opening ranking. My reservation is comparative. Game theory has been recognised repeatedly, as Fredriksson and Krusell note, and the model's empirical bite is limited. Maturity alone does not decide between candidates whose validity is uncontested. I value work whose measurement and causal content can be examined against data. I also think Binmore's place should be settled before any B001 configuration is finalised, though I follow the majority in leaving him out.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B013 first (Helpman, Grossman). He says Katz's role in B002 is real but belongs more to B038 and to the Moving to Opportunity experiment itself.
responses.response: That supports my move away from Katz on B002. On B013 I did not rank the entry. The theory of trade protection treats political influence through a compact lobbying-contribution mechanism. As a political scientist I find the measurement and empirical support for that mechanism thin, and Fredriksson himself notes the support is mixed. Its influence is not in doubt. I would still need more evidence before treating it as having had a transformative empirical effect.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats mobility measurement and causal place effects as one discovery, and how far the descriptive atlas work and the causal exposure-effects work should be credited separately.
The final choice of third laureate between Friedman and Katz. Katz's claim is real and overlaps B038, and Friedman's claim depends on how the data-infrastructure role is weighed.
Durability of the causal neighbourhood estimates, given limited independent replication on restricted data.
Whether a single-achievement prize is better than any two-part configuration, since the three-person cap prevents pairing B002 with another full candidate.
How much the 2024 institutions-and-technology prize should weigh against B038 compared with B002.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for the preferred B002 part. The supplied profile shows no collaboration with Chetty, Hendren, Friedman or Katz. The profile does list a co-author named Persson on a corruption paper, without a first name, and B027 includes Torsten Persson. B027 is not in my configuration or alternatives, and I make no claim about the identity. Stockholm University colleagues on the committee work in a different department.
